title: The gunship's third weapon is the MK-9: a modelled TALON released from the belly that falls two seconds, ignites and dives onto the painted cell
context: Owner, playtesting the live build on 2026-09-16: 'the Gunship should fire an actual missile, one of our large ones. We see it drop, then it ignites after 2 seconds and heads down (for Weapon #3, mini nuke).' Weapon 3 was the 105: GUNSHIP_GUNS.heavy with strike:true, a tracer line drawn from the muzzle to the ground over travel 3.5 s, then executeStrike at the orbital strike's own blastCells and the howitzer-blast module. Nothing modelled left the aircraft. The drop-then-ignite shape already existed for the Quiver's TALON in src/domain/missile-flight.js (eject/coast/fall/ignite/climb, its pop-out capped at OPENING_METRES = 8 on the same day).
outcome: Weapon 3 is the MK-9 mini nuke, a pooled TALON body in the world. THE BODY: the missile kit's large mesh (1,340 triangles against the DART's 188, authored for 'single special rounds / close views'), already pinned and already pooled for the Quiver's heavy shot, so no asset was added; four metres nose to tail (GUNSHIP_NUKE.length). THE FLIGHT extends src/domain/missile-flight.js rather than adding a second model: dropFrame/sampleDrop/DROP_PHASES reuse missileFrame's frame (forward/right/metre) and the sampler's { position, direction, ignition, phase } contract, which is what src/missile-presentation.js poses a pooled round from and what drives the kit's exhaust; only the curve is replaced, inverted. The authored opening is a stylised local-unit parabola, but a round let go 340 m up must fall real metres for a real two seconds, so the unpowered leg is ballistics (p = from + v0.t - up.g.t^2/2) and the powered leg a cubic Hermite entered at the fall's own velocity, so nothing kinks at ignition, and arriving straight down at arrivalLead x the distance left, so speed climbs into impact. The clock is SECONDS, not a normalised u: the free fall does not stretch with range. Every number is a parameter and src/content/gunship.js owns them: freeFall 2, drive 1.8 (travel 3.8 s), gravity 9.81, ejectSpeed 6 m/s down, arrivalLead 1.5, up passed by the caller so down is toward the planet's centre. THE NUMBERS CHANGED FOR THE 105: label 105MM -> MK-9; blastCells and dangerCells 3.2 -> 5.5 (55 m, against the 105's 32 m); travel 3.5 -> 3.8, now composed of the free fall and the drive rather than authored; reload 14 -> 20 and a new perPass 1, so the heaviest tool the seat owns is one release a station pass (src/domain/gunship.js heavySpent/heavyPass, phase 'spent'); heavyState's 'falling' split into 'released' (motor cold) and 'ignited'; the blast is EXPLOSION_USES['gunship.nuke'] (orbital-strike at 0.8, ~72 m and 10 s, against the 105's 45 m) with EXPLOSION_SCARE 10 cells / 4 s against 6 / 2.5, and executeStrike takes an explicit blastCells so the nuke's radius is its own rather than the strike tune's. EXPLOSION_USES['gunship.heavy'] is kept but no longer reachable from the gun. FRIENDLY DAMAGE IS NOT MADE SAFE: the 55 m radius breaks our own walls and sentries exactly as the strike does (strikeTune.breakWalls/breakTowers unchanged), and the warning is moved forward - from the moment a cell is painted and all the way down while the round falls, the optic rings stand on the round's cell rather than the live aim, the HUD 'In blast' reports that cell, and a red DANGER CLOSE banner over the reticle names the walls, sentries, tank or Isao standing in it. THE SEAT: src/fx/gunship-drop.js owns the presentation only (release, tick, pool) while src/domain/gunship.js stays the single clock for the impact, so the body and the damage cannot drift; the GROUND TRUTH feed rides the round (a new feedLabel/feedBack/feedLift on the mesh lets it ask for a camera 13 m above itself looking down, because the seeker's behind-the-round framing puts the sky behind a falling body) and then frames the blast; the HUD reads ARMED / PAINTED / RELEASED / IGNITED / IMPACT / SPENT.
alternatives: A second flight model for the drop, separate from missile-flight.js: rejected - the phase vocabulary, the frame and the pose contract are the same, and a second model would need its own pooling and exhaust rules.

Keeping the authored local-unit parabola for the unpowered leg: rejected - it scales with range, so a two-second fall from 340 m would not be two seconds of real fall, which is exactly the number the owner gave.

Re-timing the powered Hermite for acceleration the way the pop-up's course() does: rejected - re-timing breaks the velocity match at ignition; the arrival tangent (arrivalLead) gives the same acceleration with no kink.

Letting the round keep only the aircraft's velocity: tried and seen to fail in the first browser strip - it drifted out of the sight within a second. It is ejected six metres a second straight down now, so from the seat it drops away down the sight.
Reusing the 105's howitzer-blast for the yield: rejected - the owner asked for a mini nuke, and the module list already pins a nuclear-size explosion.
evidence: Owner note, 2026-09-16, playtesting the live build.
npm test (120 test programs passed) and npm run check green on each commit.

test/missile-flight.mjs: the drop profile's free fall is unpowered ballistics for exactly freeFall seconds, the motor is cold until then and lit after, no jump at the catch, unit nose the whole way, nose-down arrival, exact arrival on the point, metre and up both scale it.
test/gunship.mjs: ready -> painted -> released -> ignited -> impact -> reloading -> spent, one release a pass, and a fresh round on the next pass.
test/explosions-content.mjs: gunship.nuke out-yields gunship.heavy by more than 1.4x, stays under strike.orbital, and scatters the swarm wider and longer.

scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --gunship: PASS, with the five-frame strip artifacts/browser/gunship-nuke-{release,freefall,ignite,dive,blast}.png read by eye. The first run showed a black GROUND TRUTH box at release (the feed rode behind a round whose nose was horizontal, so the sky was the backdrop) and the round sliding out of the sight; both fixed and re-run green.
src/td-tab.js unchanged in line count (13,505, its budget): the wiring went into existing lines and the presentation into the new src/fx/gunship-drop.js.
